toegepas.voor: daarom maak baie wewers hulle klam
toegepas.na: daarom maak baie wewers die halms klam
toegepas.rede_vinder: Directly after 'baie wewers', 'hulle' can be read as the weavers themselves; naming the stalks makes the reference clear.
toegepas.fout: 'hulle' directly follows 'baie wewers', so the nearest antecedent is the weavers rather than the stalks.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming the stalks fixes a pronoun that could point to two antecedents, and the meaning stays the same.

laat_vaar.blok: Werk wat al honderde jare aanhou
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: As written, 'uit gras' can be read as applying to the clay pots too; the compound removes the ambiguity without changing the meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: No reader takes clay pots to be made of grass, so 'mandjies uit gras' already reads naturally and the compound is a lateral move on a sentence the previous round already settled.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Bo-op mekaar' is the natural Afrikaans for layers lying one on top of the other.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'In dik lae op mekaar' is natural Afrikaans and means the same as 'bo-op mekaar', so the swap is lateral.

laat_vaar.voor: Klei is sag genoeg om te vorm
laat_vaar.na: Klei is sag genoeg om dit te vorm
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Vorm' needs an object here; without 'dit' it can read as the clay forming by itself.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Sag genoeg om te vorm' is the normal Afrikaans construction with an understood object, like 'maklik om te lees', and adding 'dit' does not improve it.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Bakstene begin ook by nat klei.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Bakstene begin ook as nat klei.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'begin by' means start at a place; 'begin as' is the natural way to say bricks start out as wet clay.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Begin by' (the process starts from wet clay) is natural Afrikaans, while 'begin as' says the brick is wet clay at first, which fits badly with the sand and straw added a sentence later.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Groen halms krimp later in die mandjie.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Groen halms sou later in die mandjie krimp.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The sentence gives the reason for drying first; 'sou' makes clear it is what would happen to green stalks, not what happens to the dried ones in the basket.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original states plainly what green stalks do, and that already gives the reason for drying; 'sou' turns a fact into a hypothetical and adds nothing a Grade 5 reader needs.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Singular 'palmblaar' used as a mass noun reads unnatural; the plural is the usual form.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Palmblaar' used as a mass noun names the material, which is natural; the plural suggests whole leaves and shifts what is described.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Vir baie matte bind gare die halms langs mekaar vas.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Vir baie matte word die halms met gare langs mekaar vasgebind.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Making the thread the subject that ties is wooden; the passive with 'met gare' is the natural construction and keeps the meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Thread as the subject that ties is acceptable Afrikaans, and the proposed passive is longer and no clearer for a Grade 5 reader.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: is sterker as een halm alleen.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'enige halm' can be read as any stalk at all, including those in the mat; 'een halm alleen' says clearly a single loose stalk.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Sterker as enige halm' is natural and clear in context; the proposal rewords a comparative claim without a real fault to fix.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: hou daardie nat buitekant ver van die binnekant af.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: hou daardie nat buitekant weg van die binnekant.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'iets weg hou van' is the natural idiom for keeping something away; 'ver van ... af hou' reads stiff.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Ver van ... af hou' is idiomatic Afrikaans and 'ver' carries the distance the thick layer gives, which 'weg van' drops.
